facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s who was a never-smoker
presented with an enlarged, firm right ala
a lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa 5 years prior
biopsied and reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative
recurrence of the lesion 8 months prior to presentation
the lesion was excised but recurred quickly after 2 months
tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
p63 positive and p16 negative, with positive margins
thicker right ala compared with the left ala
Downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma
reflected ala after lateral rhinotomy showing tumor in ala and its extension into the floor of the nasal vestibule

concepts.why: The patient's initial biopsy was reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma, and subsequent excisions also showed similar characteristics.
The patient's tumor showed characteristics of a sweat gland origin, and the presence of atypical keratinocytes and positive margins suggests a malignant transformation.
The patient's tumor showed characteristics of a sweat gland origin, and the presence of a firm, enlarged ala suggests a possible cylindroma.
The patient's tumor showed characteristics of a hidradenoma, and the presence of positive margins and recurrence suggests a possible malignant transformation.
The patient's tumor showed characteristics of a sweat gland origin, and the presence of downward papillomatous proliferation suggests a possible syringocystadenoma papilliferum.
The uncovered finding of p63 positivity, pancytokeratin positivity, and p16 negativity explains the diagnosis of Hidradenoma papilliferum.
